Purpose and exclusions

Replicate a shared server clock epoch and weather state, then let clients render lighting and transitions locally. Fishing/resource modifiers read the authoritative weather/time version, not a client sky material.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create DA_Weather_Rillmere with Clear/Overcast/Rain transitions and a day-light curve. Place BP_WorldClock once in each zone; authority publishes state through GameState/component.
  2. Create local lighting/weather presentation components with capped Niagara/emitter counts and scalability options. Keep weather visuals off dedicated-server render paths.
  3. Bind WBP_HUD to weather/time text/icon cues. Reopen fishing/resource definitions only when enabling specific modifiers with a versioned rule.
  4. Test midday/night, transition join, low effects setting and server restart using accelerated development clock values.
  5. Record real-world UTC versus game-time semantics in save schema; do not persist a different clock in each player SaveGame.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Shared time, lighting, weather and biome modifiers. Rule owner: URPGWorldClockComponent. This asset’s role is Replicate a shared server clock epoch and weather state, then let clients render lighting and transitions locally. Fishing/resource modifiers read the authoritative weather/time version, not a client sky material.

  1. Zone initializes world epoch/cycle policy from backend/world configuration and publishes a compact synchronized time snapshot.
  2. Server selects a permitted biome weather transition and increments revision; clients interpolate light/fog/rain from accepted start/end.
  3. Gameplay action captures the relevant time/weather revision at its declared sampling point. Fishing pool modifiers do not change mid-transaction because a local rain effect loaded late.
  4. Late joiner receives current state and transition times, not a multicast history replay.
  5. Server restart resumes the persisted/derived cycle policy without multiple immediate weather events or reset exploits.
  6. NPC schedules may later consume time buckets, but core vendors remain recoverably accessible and no ecosystem simulation is required.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / ClockProbe / Weather_Rain / Water_Rill. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Client changes system clock -> no gameplay yield change.
Late join during storm -> same state/time interpolation, not clear until next event.
Weather definition missing -> safe Clear fallback for presentation and disable gameplay modifier with diagnostic.
Restart during transition -> consistent resumed/derived state, no repeated world-event reward.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
